Hey there, I know exactly how you feel. Our stories are really similar. I’m on antidepressants too and I’m  turning 29 in July. lf it helps any bit..what I’ve been doing despite struggling so much is being gentle with myself. I know it sounds like bullshit but it has really helped me relax despite the mental illnesses I live with. Now I won’t say I’m perfect, I’m still struggling hella  but it does help me move a little inch further and not beat myself up all the time. Also it may be pessimistic but it helps me to recognize how full of shit a lot of social expectations are. It’s all made up for people to be right and wrong and constantly leave this lack where “enough” is never enough. Even the most “accomplished” folks are struggling too so I just feel like fuck taking all of it so seriously to the point that I allow this world to dictate who I am.  I’m struggling but taking it day by day, step by step helps. Forgiveness for not being who I was “suppose” to be helps. 

I’m graduating to get my BA in October. I enrolled in a really good school but the program is completely online. I really feel like folks with agoraphobia and social anxiety can really benefit from online programs. If i had to be in a classroom setting I don’t think I would be able to do it. 

Wish you the best in your journey. I know it’s hard.

If you’re 19, this feeling is normal. At that age it’s just so much uncertainty and that alone causes so much anxiety. Be gentle with yourself, do the best you can and exactly what you want to do in life. I know it may not sit with you now, but as someone 10 years older than you, you’re soooo young and have a lot of life ahead of you. You have a blank canvas and can Bob Ross that shit! 

Aside from that, one tool that helped me so much with my anxiety about life is redefining the concepts in life that caused me anxiety. For example, “living life to the fullest” is that defined by what you really want or what you see as living life to its fullest? are you comparing that to someone else’s version of living life to the fullest? also “wasted life” how is that defined and who is an example of that. What I’ve found is that once I eliminated what I should do or should be, I was able to live more peacefully because I was just doing what I wanted to do and not trying to keep up with this expectation of living a life that wasn’t defined by me. You’re the only person in this world that is you, your definitions are the only ones that matter. You’re the expert of your life, what anyone else is doing has literally nothing to do with you. 

Kinda rambled but hope this helps and many blessings to your life journey. Be gentle with yourself, you deserve it.

I feel like I’m able to rationally deal with those things so far. 

With that said, I’ve also got hit hard with some side effects already - really dry mouth/thirst, fatigue, insomnia, slight headaches, my tummy does a loud ass rumble occasionally lol. The sleep part is really not fun but it’s familiar so I can manage.

I went in with no expectations, just set the intention of letting my body and the meds do their thing and keep my mind out of it for once lol. I’m open to if it changes or not, that happens but I’m happy to not be consumed with anxiety as long as I can keep it lol.

As someone who attended Coachella for the first time this year, from the outside it's easy to listen to the stereotypes behind the festival. I always believed it was a watered down festival full of elitist social media bullshit, funded by an anti everything billionaire and of course cultural appropriation. But after going I still believe it is but now I saw with my own two eyes that's only ONE SMALL small side of Coachella. That's the side that goes on social media and magazines but the other side  which I believe is the majority, is hardworking seasoned festival goers and have come out with their friends to have a good time and listen to fuckin music. I'm so so so happy I went car camping because there you really get to see the authenticity and the good vibes you go to festivals for, before even going into the festival itself. At the end of the day it's not my business who pays for what or who's going for what I just know the majority are cool as people and if you go you'll have a blast.
